title: Pixelproof host judgement result v1
description: `judge-result-<round>.json` — the verdicts as submitted (ADR 0009 §2), versioned by ADR 0014 §1. This is the one envelope in the run directory whose content originates OUTSIDE this tool, which is why it ships a schema document: something else has to be able to produce a valid one. What a submitter sends is the same shape minus this envelope's bookkeeping — `runId`, `nonce`, `checksDigest` and `response` — and the nonce is deliberately not carried into the persisted record. It was proven at submit time and its job is done; writing a used identity secret into retained evidence would leave it lying around in every archived run directory for no further benefit.

response.description: Exactly what `parseJudgeResponse()` accepts. A response must answer the exact checks that were asked, one result per check: a partial answer silently treated as complete is indistinguishable from a pass (ADR 0010). An `ok: false` response finalises the run as rejected, not as a skipped tier — a judge that errored produced no verdicts, and no verdicts is not a pass.

verdict.description: Tri-state. `unsure` is never promoted to `pass`; it resolves through `onUnsure` to escalation or failure, never to accepted.

evidence.description: One line naming what was actually seen. A verdict without evidence is the summary opinion this project exists to stop trusting.
